task_instance: Build a minimal TypeScript MCP server ('task-manager') implementing the MCP Server Development Guide's core deliverable: an MCP server exposing well-designed tools (task_add, task_list, task_complete) with Zod input/output schemas, annotations (readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint), structuredContent, and actionable error messages, following the Phase 2/3 guidance (TypeScript SDK, stdio transport, npm build verification, and functional testing with a real MCP client in place of the interactive MCP Inspector).
evidence: Project at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/anthropics__skills__mcp-builder/mcp-taskserver. Installed @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod, typescript, @types/node via npm (all succeeded, 0 vulnerabilities). Wrote src/index.ts implementing an McpServer with 3 tools (task_add, task_list with pagination/filtering, task_complete) using registerTool with Zod inputSchema/outputSchema and MCP tool annotations, connected via StdioServerTransport. Ran `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json` -> compiled cleanly to dist/index.js (BUILD_OK). Wrote test-client.mjs using the MCP TypeScript SDK's Client + StdioClientTransport to actually spawn the server process and drive it over the real MCP protocol: listTools() returned all 3 registered tools; callTool for task_add created tasks with correct structuredContent; task_list returned correct filtered/paginated results with structuredContent {tasks, total}; task_complete correctly mutated state and returned isError:true with an actionable message for an invalid id. Full transcript captured in the command output above, confirming the server behaves correctly as an installable, testable MCP server. No external API, network access, credentials, or paid/account-bound services were needed since the sample task-manager domain uses in-memory state, so no safety boundary was hit. Evaluation/Phase-4 XML-question authoring (subjective judgment task) and use of the interactive `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` UI (needs a browser-driven interactive session) were not exercised, but the skill's core deliverable -- producing and verifying a working MCP server with well-designed tools -- was fully achieved and verified programmatically.
